title: PM MITRA MEGA TEXTILE PARKS
body_text:
To develop integrated large scale and modern industrial infrastructure facility for entire value-chain of the textile industry, the Government has approved setting up of 7 (Seven) PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks in Greenfield/Brownfield sites with scheme outlay of Rs. 4,445 Crore for the period 2021-22 to 2027-28. The Government has finalised 7 sites viz. Tamil Nadu (Virudhnagar), Telangana (Warangal), Gujarat (Navsari), Karnataka (Kalaburagi), Madhya Pradesh (Dhar), Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow) and Maharashtra (Amravati) for setting up PM MITRA Parks. After completion, each PM MITRA Park is expected to generate approximately 3 lakh employment (1 lakh direct and 2 lakh indirect).
At present, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with all States and 100% land has been acquired for all the sites. Environmental Clearances have been received for all PM MITRA Parks. Joint Venture Agreements have been signed and SPVs incorporated for all 5 Greenfield sites. DPRs amounting to ₹13,537 crore have been finalized for all 7 States. Investment interests amounting to ₹68,590 crore have been received so far by the PM MITRA States.
State-wise details of land acquired/available, investment proposals received under the Scheme are placed below.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Textiles informed Lok Sabha that the government has approved 7 PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks with a scheme outlay of Rs. 4,445 crore for 2021-22 to 2027-28, located in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. MoUs have been signed with all states, 100% land acquired, and Environmental Clearances received for all parks, with DPRs worth Rs. 13,537 crore finalized and investment interest of Rs. 68,590 crore received so far. Each park is expected to generate about 3 lakh jobs (1 lakh direct, 2 lakh indirect).
enrichment.context:
The PM MITRA scheme, launched in 2021, aims to create world-class textile infrastructure hubs on the '5F' vision (Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign) to boost India's textile competitiveness, attract large investments, and integrate the entire textile value chain from spinning to garmenting under one roof. It follows the model of successful industrial cluster schemes and is intended to reduce logistics costs, promote ease of doing business, and help India compete with countries like Bangladesh and Vietnam in textile exports. The parks include a mix of greenfield (new) and brownfield (existing) sites, reflecting a strategy to leverage both new industrial corridors and revive underutilized textile hubs like Warangal (Telangana) and Amravati (Maharashtra), historically significant textile regions.

This scheme is significant for India's 'Make in India' and export promotion goals, given textiles is a major employment-generating sector, especially for women and rural workers. It ties into broader government efforts such as the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for textiles and the National Technical Textiles Mission, aiming to position India as a global textile manufacturing hub.

Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign (5F)
Make in India, Zero Defect Zero Effect
prelims_questions.explanation: The PM MITRA scheme is based on the '5F' vision - Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign - aimed at integrating the entire textile value chain.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following PM MITRA Park sites is classified as a Brownfield site?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, Telangana (Warangal) and Maharashtra (Amravati) are the two Brownfield sites among the 7 PM MITRA Parks, while the rest are Greenfield sites.
